name: Cardiofaciocutaneous Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Cardiofaciocutaneous Syndrome

criteria.description: Distinctive craniofacial features including high forehead, bitemporal narrowing, and downslanting palpebral fissures
Presence of congenital heart defects such as pulmonic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Skin abnormalities including sparse, curly hair, ichthyosis, and hyperkeratosis
Pathogenic mutation in BRAF, MEK1 (MAP2K1), or MEK2 (MAP2K2) genes
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major clinical features (facial dysmorphism, cardiac defects, and cutaneous abnormalities) with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is strongly recommended to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from related RASopathies.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes high forehead, bitemporal narrowing, and downslanting palpebral fissures
Commonly pulmonic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

common.notes: Poor growth in infancy and early childhood
Poor suck and swallowing problems in infancy

occasional.notes: Occur in a subset of patients

rare.notes: Severe refractory seizures in rare cases

laboratory: Possible elevated liver enzymes in some cases
imaging: Echocardiography showing pulmonic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in BRAF gene (~75% of cases)
Pathogenic variants in MEK1 (MAP2K1) or MEK2 (MAP2K2) genes
other: Characteristic facial photographs aid clinical diagnosis

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring early intervention
references: Rauen KA. The RASopathies. Annu Rev Genomics Hum Genet. 2013;14:355-369.
Niihori T, Aoki Y, Ohashi H, et al. Germline KRAS and BRAF mutations in cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome. Nat Genet. 2006;38(3):294-296.
Tartaglia M, Gelb BD. Disorders of dysregulated signal traffic through the RAS-MAPK pathway: phenotypic spectrum and molecular mechanisms. Ann N Y Acad Sci. 2010;1214:99-121.
